sources.title: Zo werken wij - de 7 stappen van Highbiza
Veiligheid en stabiliteit van jouw webshop
Zo beloon je klanten met spaarpunten in je webshop
Katapull breidt Commerce Hub uit met overname van Picqer

items.title: Highbiza is a two-decade-old Hengelo company that joined Katapull in 2025
items.summary: Started over twenty years ago as UWKM, rebranded to Highbiza in 2019 to focus on e-commerce and complex platforms, and joined the Katapull group in 2025. It shares its Hengelo address (Industrieplein 1) with Logic4.
items.implication: Group membership adds continuity and cross-sell; the product should integrate with siblings first rather than duplicate them.

items.title: Four fixed packages with hard limits drive upgrades
items.summary: Launch from EUR 149/month (+EUR 1,490 one-off; 2,500 products, 100 orders/month, 3 filters, 3 users), Core from EUR 299 (+3,490; 15,000 products, 400 orders, 6 filters, multi-shop and B2B optional, 5 users), Prestige from EUR 599 (+5,490; 50,000 products, 850 orders, 10 filters, Elastic search Ultimate, B2B module included, 10 users) and Enterprise from EUR 1,149 (unlimited, dedicated hosting, 15 users).
items.implication: Order and product limits are the natural upgrade trigger; B2B buyers in wholesale need at least Core with the B2B option.

items.title: Open-source Django stack positioned against Magento, WooCommerce and Shopify
items.summary: Highbiza builds on Django (Python), Django Oscar and Wagtail CMS, claiming no licence costs or vendor lock-in, and contrasts itself with Magento (heavy), WooCommerce (plug-in dependent) and Shopify (limited customisation, app-store dependent). It reports many customers arriving after years on Magento or WooCommerce.
items.implication: Replatforming from overgrown open-source shops is the primary acquisition path; migration quality is a core capability.

items.title: A library of 100+ reusable building blocks is the delivery model
items.summary: Shops are composed from more than 100 building blocks (FAQ, customer portal, staffel prices, stock, filters); many are included, extensions cost a fixed monthly fee, and custom work is quoted. Because shops are standardised, a fix in one block benefits every shop using it.
items.implication: Every new requirement should first be framed as a reusable block; custom code erodes the maintenance advantage.

items.title: Published customer counts differ between pages
items.summary: highbiza.nl states '420 websites & webshops' (home), 'ruim 400 websites en webshops' and '250+ handelsorganisaties' (klanten), '250+ bedrijven' (prijzen) and '150+ organisaties' (over Highbiza).
items.implication: Treat Highbiza's base as roughly 150-250 organisations running about 400 sites; do not use a single precise figure.

items.title: Wholesale features: customer prices, staffels, quotes, reorder and ERP integration
items.summary: For wholesalers Highbiza lists customer-specific prices and assortments, staffel discounts and net price lists, Elastic Search, quotes and order repetition, and integrations with ERP, PIM and accounting; for technical wholesalers also specifications, datasheets, multilingual content and integrations with Exact, Business Central or Logic4.
items.implication: The B2B module and ERP integration are the heart of the wholesale proposition.

items.title: Katapull siblings already appear as Highbiza integrations
items.summary: The integrations page lists Logic4 and Vendit (ERP category), EffectConnect (marketplace integrators) and DeliveryMatch (carriers), each described as part of Katapull, next to Exact Online, Business Central, Gripp, Prima, MediaMagic, seven payment providers and carriers such as Sendcloud, MyParcel, PostNL, Trunkrs and Royal Mail. No Returnista or Transus integration is listed.
items.implication: Cross-brand connectors are a real asset; Returnista and Transus are gaps to fill for returns and EDI.

items.title: Loods28: from Magento to tens of thousands of orders a year
items.summary: Loods28 (Neede) moved from a Magento shop that could not cope to Highbiza in 2021 (Core package). It reports 50,000-100,000 orders a year with peaks of 2,000 a week, more than 7,000 direct customers excluding marketplaces, and sales through its own shop, bol and Amazon; business customers are the fastest-growing segment.
items.implication: Mixed B2B/B2C e-tailers with marketplace sales are a key segment; marketplace integration and order-volume scaling matter.

items.title: HR Premium Parts became a launch customer for Highbiza and Logic4 together
items.summary: HR Premium Parts (Twello) has run its shop on Highbiza since 2015 (Prestige). In 2023 it became a launch customer for both Highbiza and Logic4, cleaning up product data, customer groups and stock and adding real-time dashboards.
items.implication: Joint Highbiza + Logic4 go-lives are a proven pattern; data clean-up is the main effort.

items.title: Kroon-Oil chose Highbiza in a tender for marketing self-service and performance
items.summary: Lubricant producer Kroon-Oil (Enterprise package) ran a tender with three agencies for performance, scalability, cloud and a CMS marketing could run itself; it launched its renewed site on 20 August 2024 and runs several brands (Kroon-Oil, VatOil, Putoline) on one base. Menu changes that took weeks now take days.
items.implication: Self-service CMS and multi-brand capability win marketing-led evaluations.

items.title: Katapull is building an operational commerce hub and keeps acquiring
items.summary: Katapull (Rotterdam) presents eight labels in its Commerce Hub - Vendit, Logic4, Highbiza, EffectConnect, DeliveryMatch, Transus, Returnista and, since October 2026, Picqer (WMS) - with 175+ specialists, 4,500+ customers in 40+ countries, 27,500+ users and 140+ marketplaces. Its CEO says the focus is the operational side of commerce: orders, stock, logistics and returns.
items.implication: Highbiza is the group's storefront and digital-growth label; its value rises when it plugs into the operational brands.

items.title: Quality is automated: nightly tests, screenshot diffs, security checks, daily backups, ISO 27001
items.summary: Highbiza automates system management, makes daily backups, runs Jenkins functional tests, screenshot comparisons and security checks every night, applies a four-eyes principle and holds ISO 27001 certification; support requests are handled within one working day.
items.implication: Managed operations are a differentiator against self-hosted open-source shops and must stay visible to customers.

items.title: Consumer features added in 2026: loyalty points and a withdrawal form
items.summary: In February 2026 Highbiza described a loyalty points system with merchant-set earn and burn ratios; in July 2026 it published how to create a Return Form Page so consumers can use their 14-day withdrawal right online.
items.implication: The platform serves D2C and retail too; consumer-law compliance and retention features matter for those shops.
